primarySource.citation: Paller, V. G. V., Corpuz, M. N. C., & Bandal, M. Z. Jr. (2017). Freshwater fish assemblages and water quality parameters in Seven Lakes of San Pablo, Laguna, Philippines. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 8(1), 1-22. https://doi.org/10.7828/ajob.v8i1.995
primarySource.access: The official publisher page and all 22 pages of the official PDF were readable through web extraction during this 2026-10-30 recheck. No local PDF or page image was retained. An earlier check had encountered an interactive PDF challenge; this successful recheck used the publisher's exposed PDF text and did not bypass a gate.
sourceFactsReviewed: The study names the seven San Pablo lakes and reports 5,166 fish individuals, ten species and six families in aggregate.
The methods state monthly sampling from February 2013 through January 2014 and April 2014 through March 2015, using local fisherfolk and scoop/gill nets.
The article's narrative identifies the Bunot carp as Carassius gibelio; the plate caption also labels a specimen Carassius gibelio.

The PDF's appendix caption identifies Table 2 as the per-lake freshwater fish distribution table, but the extracted text did not expose the table cells and no cell-by-cell transcription was made in this review.
primarySource.reuseReview: No item-specific license or rights grant was found on the article page or in the reviewed PDF text. The publisher's current manuscript-submission guidance says authors must submit a signed Mandatory Copyright Transfer, but the signed agreement for this 2017 article was not available. Do not reproduce or project the species table without item-specific permission.

secondarySource.citation: Paller, V. G. V. et al. (2021). The Seven Lakes of San Pablo: Assessment and Monitoring Strategies Toward Sustainable Lake Ecosystems. Philippine Science Letters, 14(1), 158-179. https://doi.org/10.54645/2021141DFX-14
sourceFactsReviewed: The paper describes itself as a review of monitoring and research published from 1990 through 2020, not a new fish-assemblage field survey.
Its discussion attributes the same seven-lake, ten-species survey to Paller et al. (2017a), and reports the Bunot carp as Carassius carassius.
The 2021 article is secondary literature and cannot independently confirm the species identity or override the cited primary source.
secondarySource.access: The official journal page and complete 22-page PDF were readable through web extraction; no local copy was retained.
secondarySource.reuseReview: No item-specific license or rights grant was found on the article page or in the reviewed PDF text. No permission to reproduce the review's text, tables, or figures is inferred.

officialProjectMetadata.projectTitle: Diversity and Ecology of Acanthocephala Parasites in Freshwater Fishes from the Seven Lakes of San Pablo City, Philippines
officialProjectMetadata.implementingAgency: University of the Philippines Los Baños, Institute of Biological Sciences
sourceFactsReviewed: The public NRCP/DOST page records project E-224 as completed and cleared, led by Paller at UPLB.
Its project summary lists Carassius carassius and states that wild fish were collected from all Seven Lakes; it gives no specimen voucher details for the carp in the reviewed text.

The project page's fish collection window overlaps the Seven Lakes assemblage study, but the relationship between the parasite project samples and the 2017 article's carp identification is not established. This is not independent evidence resolving the identity conflict.
The inspected project page linked no final report or data file and its footer states NRCP copyright with all rights reserved.
officialProjectMetadata.reuseReview: No item-specific fish-data reuse permission was found. Do not turn the project summary's named fish into a structured occurrence dataset.

taxonomicCrossCheck.authority: Eschmeyer's Catalog of Fishes, California Academy of Sciences
taxonomicCrossCheck.interpretation: The two names are not synonyms in the checked authority. This confirms that the source wording conflict is material; taxonomy does not identify the collected Bunot specimen or determine which paper's field identification is correct.

decision: Keep all per-lake fish rows held. The 2017 primary source's item-specific reuse terms remain unresolved. The Bunot Carassius identity conflicts across the 2017 primary article, 2021 secondary review, and NRCP/DOST project metadata; the latter two are not independent confirmation, and no reviewed source provides a voucher-level resolution. Treat secondary/project pages as context and provenance, not alternate occurrence sources.
nextAction: Reopen only with item-specific reuse permission and source-level evidence that resolves the Bunot carp identification (for example, an author correction, voucher/specimen record, or independent eligible survey). Otherwise pursue independently reusable site-resolved records; do not treat the old survey or the bounded GBIF checks as current lake inventories.
